queries.rationale: What single condition explains acute steroid-responsive proximal myalgia with markedly raised CK, lifelong exertional intolerance, and exertional muscle spasms?
The childhood 50-yard-sprint collapse and adult exertional spasms suggest a long-standing underlying mechanism the acute presentation unmasked.
Markedly exertion-provoked CK elevation (811 baseline rising to 3473) is a pivotal distinguishing feature pointing toward an exertion-sensitive muscle process.
Onset anchored to three months after a diabetes diagnosis; causal/unmasking/coincidental is a question the framing invites.
Given negative serology, normal spine MRI, and nondiagnostic muscle MRI, what further test would secure the diagnosis?
Whether the prednisolone response argues for or against the unifying diagnosis.
